## Question

How can a Shiny app use periodically updated data without being redeployed
each time the data changes?

An app can query a database or API directly, or carry a static dataset in its
deployment bundle. Slowly changing data offers another option: prepare a
snapshot separately, publish it somewhere accessible, and let the app read it.

## Experiment

I built a [Northeast Ohio Home Value Explorer](https://mpfoley73.shinyapps.io/neohio-home-values/)
using public [Zillow Research data](https://www.zillow.com/research/data/).
Visitors compare up to four of ten local communities, choose a starting year,
and switch between estimated typical home values and percentage growth.

```text
Zillow city CSV
  -> publish-data.R: select, reshape, validate
  -> board/: versioned pin and _pins.yaml manifest
  -> Quarto copies resources into docs/
  -> commit and push -> GitHub Pages deployment
  -> shinyapps.io app reads the public pin per visitor session
```

### Prepare and pin locally

The publisher downloads the all-homes, mid-tier, smoothed, seasonally adjusted
Zillow Home Value Index (ZHVI). It selects ten Ohio communities and reshapes
the monthly columns into `community`, `date`, and `value`. Checks require the
requested communities, unique community/month pairs, valid dates, and positive
nonmissing values. Missing observations are preserved.

The essential artifact handoff is:

```r
board <- pins::board_folder(board_path, versioned = TRUE)

pins::pin_write(
  board,
  housing_long,
  name = "home-values",
  type = "rds",
  metadata = list(source_url = source_url)
)

housing_pinned <- pins::pin_read(board, "home-values")
stopifnot(identical(housing_long, housing_pinned))
pins::write_board_manifest(board)
```

These are reference snippets; the complete publisher is `publish-data.R`.
RDS preserves R column types, including `Date`. The round-trip check verifies
that the saved artifact matches the prepared object.

The **board** is the storage folder; `home-values` is a named **pin** within it:

```text
board/
  _pins.yaml
  home-values/
    <version>/
      data.txt
      home-values.rds
```

### Make the board accessible online

Writing a pin creates local files; it does not publish them. A web reader
cannot inspect a directory like a local filesystem, so `_pins.yaml` lists the
pins and their version locations. Regenerate this manifest after writing pins.

The root `_quarto.yml` includes:

```yaml
project:
  resources:
    - .nojekyll
    - experiments/housing-pins/board/
```

These entries tell Quarto to copy the board and the empty `.nojekyll` file into
`docs/`. The board files are copied unchanged, rather than rendered as HTML.
`.nojekyll` tells GitHub Pages to skip Jekyll processing so underscore-prefixed
files such as `_pins.yaml` are served too.

Rendering, committing, pushing, and waiting for GitHub Pages to deploy makes
the copied board accessible over HTTPS. The resource configuration works
independently of this write-up's draft status. The publisher also makes RDS
files writable after pinning so Quarto can replace copied files on Windows.

### Read the snapshot in Shiny

The app's `server()` function contains:

```r
web_board <- pins::board_url(
  "https://mpfoley73.github.io/ds_lab/experiments/housing-pins/board/"
)
housing <- pins::pin_read(web_board, "home-values")
```

Inside `server()`, this runs once per new visitor session. Existing sessions
keep their snapshot. Outside `server()`, loading would happen at R process
startup, so subsequent visitors could keep receiving older data. Process
restarts are not our refresh mechanism. Pins caching can avoid unnecessary
downloads; this experiment has not measured cache behavior separately.

The controls filter the session's data and redraw the chart without rereading
the pin. Growth uses the first month on or after the selected start with values
for every selected community. Each line uses its own value in that shared month:

```r
plot_data <- selected_data |>
  filter(date >= baseline_date) |>
  arrange(community, date) |>
  mutate(.by = community, value = 100 * (value / first(value) - 1))
```

Every growth line starts at zero. The shared-baseline requirement applies only
to growth mode; dollar comparisons do not require overlapping observations.

## What I learned

**Preparing data, publishing data, and deploying app code are separate actions.**
The app and artifact do not need to share a hosting platform. This recreates
the separation I previously used with pins on Posit Connect, using platforms
I already had: GitHub Pages for public data and shinyapps.io for the app.
Connect-specific authentication and scheduling were not part of this experiment.

| Change | Workflow |
|---|---|
| New housing data | Run `publish-data.R`; render and review the copied board; commit and push; verify the public pin after Pages deploys |
| New app behavior | Run `deploy-app.R`, which deploys only `app/` to shinyapps.io |
| New write-up content | Render, review, and publish through the normal `ds_lab` website workflow |

Run scripts from the repository root. Follow the root README for website
publication; running the publisher alone does not update GitHub Pages.

**Verified:** the initial snapshot contains 3,210 observations across ten
communities through September 2026. Local and public pin reads reproduced the
prepared data exactly. The deployed app works with the public board. Review
also checked percentage calculations, selection limits, and a missing initial
observation shifting the common baseline.

**Pending:** when October observations become available, publish a new snapshot
and open a new app session without redeploying the app. Confirm the later data
month appears. That will complete the independent-update demonstration.

ZHVI is a modeled estimate of typical home value, not an individual appraisal
or the median price of homes sold. Historical estimates can be revised. This is
a small public-data proof of concept: no scheduler, database, automatic refresh
of open sessions, or elaborate recovery system.

For the reusable hosting pattern, see the
[pins web-hosted boards guide](https://pins.rstudio.com/articles/using-board-url.html).
